You grade a first-hour triage against what the operator's own incident review later concluded.

For each finding, decide whether a duty team following the triage (its matched rules, next actions and escalation) would have been pointed at the substance of that finding during the incident:
- "yes": the triage names it or directs the action it describes.
- "partly": the triage points in the right direction but misses the key specific (the mechanism, the order, the threshold, the person).
- "no": nothing in the triage leads there.
For remediation findings (longer-term fixes), "yes" means the triage already applies that practice.

"by" lists the rule ids that earned the credit (empty for "no"). "note" is one short sentence. Judge only from the triage given; do not reward actions the triage did not state.

Reply with JSON only: {"per_finding":[{"finding":"F1","anticipated":"yes|partly|no","by":["R-001"],"note":"..."}]}

{"triage":{"classification":"partly_recurring","matched_rules":[{"rule_id":"R-001","because":"A utility voltage sag occurred and chillers failed to restart, indicating mechanical cooling may be compromised; the rule directs verifying cooling and treating the datacenter as on a thermal buffer.","signals":["AZ-AUE-2023:S78","AZ-AUE-2023:S79"]},{"rule_id":"R-010","because":"A utility voltage sag tripped multiple chillers offline and manual restarts are required across two data halls; the rule mandates a load-based restart sequence across data halls.","signals":["AZ-AUE-2023:S78","AZ-AUE-2023:S79","AZ-AUE-2023:S81","AZ-AUE-2023:S82"]},{"rule_id":"R-012","because":"Chillers supporting the two data halls tripped offline; the rule requires counting operational chillers against the minimum (four) per data hall.","signals":["AZ-AUE-2023:S19","AZ-AUE-2023:S20","AZ-AUE-2023:S79"]},{"rule_id":"R-014","because":"A voltage event tripped multiple chillers and manual restart is required; the rule directs increasing technician staffing to execute restarts promptly.","signals":["AZ-AUE-2023:S78","AZ-AUE-2023:S79","AZ-AUE-2023:S81","AZ-AUE-2023:S82"]}],"next_actions":[{"action":"Immediately verify that mechanical cooling systems are still running; if cooling has shut down, treat the datacenter as on a load-dependent thermal buffer and start planning for its depletion.","rule_id":"R-001"},{"action":"Count how many chillers each impacted data hall still has running against its minimum requirement of four; treat any data hall below minimum as being in thermal runaway risk and act on load before temperatures climb.","rule_id":"R-012"},{"action":"Sequence manual chiller restarts by data hall load so that every impacted data hall gets partial cooling early, rather than finishing one data hall before starting the next; do not work through chillers in an adjacent sequence.","rule_id":"R-010"},{"action":"Increase technician staffing at the datacenter so manual restart procedures can be executed promptly and assign teams so restarts can proceed in parallel across data halls rather than sequentially.","rule_id":"R-014"}],"escalate":{"now":true,"to":"facility operations lead and cooling plant engineer","reason":"Mechanical cooling is confirmed shut down (13 chillers failed to restart) and multiple chillers require manual restart across more than one data hall, triggering R-001 and R-010 escalations."},"not_covered":["No rule addresses the specific scenario of a voltage sag causing 13 chillers to fail automatic restart while the site has seven chillers total (five running, two standby) and the two data halls require at least four operational chillers; the combination of exact chiller counts and restart failure is not fully covered by any single rule."]},"findings":[{"id":"F1","kind":"root_cause","text":"The voltage sag caused cooling system chillers for multiple datacenters to shut down."},{"id":"F2","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"Incremental load increases over time in the Availability Zone resulted in a chiller operating configuration that was susceptible to a timing defect in the Chiller Management System."},{"id":"F3","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"By the time the team reached the final five chillers requiring a manual restart, the water inside the pump system for these chillers (chilled water loop) had reached temperatures that were too high to allow them to be restarted."},{"id":"F4","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"In this scenario, the restart is inhibited by a self-protection mechanism that acts to prevent damage to the chiller that would occur by processing water at the elevated temperatures."},{"id":"F5","kind":"response","text":"At 11:34 UTC, as temperatures continued to increase, our onsite datacenter team began a remote shutdown of remaining networking, compute, and storage infrastructure in the impacted data halls to protect data durability, infrastructure health, and address the thermal runaway."},{"id":"F6","kind":"response","text":"This shutdown allowed the chilled water loop to return to a safe temperature which allowed us to restart the chillers."},{"id":"F7","kind":"remediation","text":"We have de-risked this failure to restart due to voltage fluctuations, by implementing a change to the control timing logic on the Chiller Management System (Completed)."},{"id":"F8","kind":"remediation","text":"Emergency Operation Procedure for manual restarts of simultaneous chiller failures has changed from an ‘adjacent’ sequence to a data hall ‘load based’ sequence to ensure all impacted data halls have partial cooling, to slow thermal runaway while full cooling is being restored (Completed)."},{"id":"F9","kind":"remediation","text":"Following this incident, as a temporary mitigation, we increased technician staffing levels at the datacenter to be prepared to execute manual restart procedures of our chillers prior to the change to the Chiller Management System to prevent restart failures."},{"id":"F10","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"Based on our incident analysis the staffing levels at the time would have been sufficient to prevent impact if a ‘load based' chiller restart sequence had been followed, which we have since implemented (Completed)."},{"id":"F11","kind":"impact","text":"At 10:30 UTC some networking, compute, and storage infrastructure began to shutdown automatically as data hall temperatures increased, impacting service availability."}]}
